notes.title: GladiEATers to feature in Creature Collector Fest!
notes.content:
[h3][b]Cook them to Collect Them! [/b][/h3]

[h3]We’re excited to announce that GladiEATers will be featured in Creature Collector Fest! 
[/h3]

This Fest is for games about collecting creatures! Fantastical creatures only – walking fruit with eyes, dogs with rockets, flying cat-fish-spider hybrids are all welcome. Extinct animals (ie. dinosaurs) are also welcome. GladiEATers fits in perfectly to this category, as you cook and collect your foodie monsters to take into battle! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/c74b8cf5d026def32cfda8d1c94008a2405acd18.jpg[/img]

Cook your team in a snappy series of bite-sized minigames, then command your culinary creations in turn-based battles. Follow a diverse cast of characters, each with their own specialities. 

Every battle begins in the kitchen! Start with basic ingredients and cook against the clock to develop them into powerful creatures. With each mini-game, you’ll change your GladiEATers’ form and boost its stats, but it’s up to you to choose how to spend your time. Will you cook up a complex-but-powerful ratatouille or overwhelm your opponent with a massive serving of simple boiled eggs?

notes.title: Dev Blog #10 – Onion Roster Design
notes.content:
[h2]Crying Powers![/h2]
	When cut, onions release a chemical called [u]lachymatory factor[/u], which contains [i]sulphur[/i]! If you’re like me, this makes me [b]cry my eyes out to a gross extent[/b] – even after years of chopping. This was our first design touchstone when it came to designing the [b]GladiEATers [/b]roster – crying.
[h2]Root Motiff[/h2]
	We think the best roster designs are formed around a [i]central image[/i]. For onions, we reinterpreted the [i][b]Eye of Horus[/b][/i] into a simplified crying eye. Blue is a colour that seemed to be associated with the eye in culture and jewllery, which made the [i]blue tear[/i] association feel very natural.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ce393e90bb697138dea6b3fc1a87369abbbe8b35.png[/img]
[h2]Eyes on eyes (on eyes)[/h2]
	Our Raw Onion [b]GladiEATer [/b]starts the roster with the motiff strong. Being a [i]bulb with eyes [/i]crying all around. It also sets the stage with the [u]most simple [b]cry[/b][/u] inducing ability:
[olist]
[*] 	[b]Tear Up:[/b] - Enemy [b]Cries[/b].	Being a weak, low time to cook, Raw creature, two of Raw Onion’s abilities are sacrificial/ make [i]Raw Onion[/i] into more of a consumable, like the Raw Egg. 
[*] 	[b]Peel Feel: [/b]- Makes an [u]ally’s next attack[/u] inflict [b]crying[/b]. - But destroys the Onion in the process.
[*] 	[b]Stembutt: [/b]- [b]Deals [/b]a small amount of damage. - [b]Takes [/b]a small amount of damage.
[/olist]
[i]How good does this make [i]Raw Onion?[/i] I wish there was some explanation of [b]what crying does…[/b][/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/281b275b2a7c984c4ba31a83e8af1011baa8390e.gif[/img]
[h2]...What crying used to do[/h2]
	Originally, [b]crying [/b]made all your abilities [u]target enemies and allies randomly[/u]. This was a natural first iteration of the mechanic, but after a few months of testing, we realised this wasn’t the sort of [i]"wow that’s fun"[/i] randomness. Instead ,it was the type of randomness that either:
[list]
[*]  Feels [b]mediocre [/b]if a crying enemy hits another, less optimal, target on your team.
[b]OR [/b]
[*]  Feels [b]bad [/b]if it hits an equally optimal target on your team [i](you’d ask, what was the point of me making them cry).[/i]
[b] OR EVEN WORSE[/b]
[*]   Feels [b][u]terrible[/u][/b] if your enemy casts an area of effect ability that targets your entire team - making your random targeting debuff [i]completely irrelevant.[/i]
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/3db8171daa3a1ba7aa7080886ec51528ff7f0406.gif[/img]
[h2]What crying does[/h2]
	Instead, we saw crying as an [b]opportunity [/b]to partly fix another problem. We were worried that some players would decide on 1 ability of the 3 a [b]GladiEATer [/b]has to be the [u]best[/u] and [i]continue casting that on repeat[/i] - without getting to have a strategic decision every turn. 
	To prevent this, we changed the crying debuff to [b]stop the player from casting the same ability twice[/b]. Now the player has the interesting situation where they are [i]forced to change up their strategy[/i], picking the best of now two of their abilities. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/4d32ec428c6e738b3df173c87f58422a902d2715.png[/img]
	This felt like a step in the right direction. However, with so many tear inducing abilities and a relatively minor effect that does not stack - what gave players a reason to make a [b]GladiEATer [/b][u]cry twice?[/u] Blocking more abilities felt too limiting for the enemy. So, what about an [b]explosion[/b].[b][i] Everyone loves explosions.[/i][/b]
	Now, when a crying [b]GladiEATer [/b]is made to cry again – the tear [u][b]explodes [/b][/u]- dealing significant damage.
Thematically, this could be interpreted as the [b]GladiEATer [/b][i]having a tantrum[/i], or getting so sad that they take damage. [i]Poor things[/i] ☹
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/c32008a7bf69d51dcfdd7983aeffb7542b5fc274.gif[/img]
[b]GladiEATers [/b]crying is represented by a tear drop under the [b]GladiEATer’s [/b]eye, which we’ve set on every single sprite [i](even those with no eyes!).[/i] Additionally, the 2nd time a [b]GladiEATer [/b]is made to cry, [b]the tear explodes[/b] as the damage activates and the crying stops.
[h2]More Onions![/h2]
	Diane’s onion creations involve chopped [i]Raw Onion Slices[/i]. These hover around [i]melancholically, [/i]with occasional [b]woeful outbursts:[/b]
[olist]
[*] 	[b]Projection: [/b]-Deal [b]damage [/b]randomly, [i]3 times! [/i][Nothing like taking your sadness out on someone random]
[*] 	[b]Teary Gaze:[/b] -Enemy [b]Cries[/b].
[*] 	[b]Peeling Bad:[/b] -[i]Lose [/i]25% Max [b]Health[/b]. –[i]Gain [/i]25% [b]Power[/b].[i] [Keeping in-line with the peeling punnage][/i]
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ddd15edfd7c966622731a090a3b25f7cbd2e317c.gif[/img]
	[i]The Grilled Onion Slice[/i] has honed its tear powers, developing… arms! This [u]groundbreaking [/u]adaptation allows it to hone its tears into [b]targeted balls of sad power.[/b]
[olist]
[*] 	[b]Teary Touch:[/b] -Deal Damage and make an enemy [b]cry [/b][strike][Not a tear Hadouken][/strike]
[*] 	[b]Spreading Sulphide:[/b] -Ally’s next attack makes targets [b]cry [/b].
[*] 	[b]Regretful Vanquish: [/b]-Charge Up. -Deal Damage equal to [b]½ of target’s missing health.[/b]
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/9946ef9a209729a6e4be34407dc8c6fc157e9485.gif[/img]
Regretful Vanquish has the [i]Grilled Onion [/i]rubbing its eyes to form a massive scounrful tear. It is great for taking down [b]high health enemies.[/b]
[b]Spreading Sulphide[/b] also synergises powerfully with abilities that target multiple enemies, such as [i]Raw Onion Slice’s[/i] Projection or even Tomato Spit which Diane’s [i]Tomato Slices[/i] have access too!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/56843f50cf7d53ff2e6c269a97f8e18c4c9bbe28.gif[/img]
[h2]Too Sad, Too Furious[/h2]
	[i]Fried Onion Rings[/i]. They’re [b]onions[/b], they [b]cry[/b], and they’re [b]fast[/b]. The Fried Onion Ring shaped like a literal tire and greased up by never ending tears, this sad speed demon only knows [u]get fast or cry trying:[/u]
[olist]
[*] 	[b]Greasy Steer: [/b]-Deal damage and [u]get faster.[/u]
[*] 	[b]Battery Burnout: [/b]-Lose life and [u]get faster.[/u]
[*] 	[b]Tear Streaks: [/b]–Draw a tear line, [[i]similar to how tire marks burn rubber on the ground][/i] - Enemies that attack allies with this line begin to [b]cry[/b].
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/78cf7cb82894ea5908ab723c0861c063ddeb1790.gif[/img]
[h2]Diane's Design Link[/h2]
	We linked Diane’s design to the onion’s by putting our augmented [i][b]Eyes of Horus[/b][/i] on her as a sleeve of tattoos. Diane’s ability of pushing her already low health (and therefore sad) [b]GladiEATers [/b]made thematic sense with her crying creatures being [i]sad to work for her[/i]. Finally, Diane [b]makes other chefs cry[/b] due to her meanness, much like her onions.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/1b162e99e5dd5618988a39eb640a0e6d7794561b.png[/img]
[h2]Oni-off [/h2]
	Saying goodbye always makes me [i]sad [/i];( Thank you for reading a bit more about our [i]crying onion buddies[/i]. There’s even more [b]GladiEATers [/b]to talk about, perhaps even onion based [b]GladiEATers [/b][i]yet to be announced??[/i]
[url=https://discord.com/invite/Bv9WxvDPag][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/66cfebe3655afc8a7b4d03af2f142e6291d637a4.png[/img][/url]
	Consider joining our [b][url=https://discord.com/invite/Bv9WxvDPag]Discord [/url][/b]or leaving a comment – that would bring a [u]tear to my eye. [/u]

notes.title: Dev Blog #9 – Deadly Combat Chef Diane
notes.content:
[h2]Who is Diane?[/h2]
For many, food is a means to [b]connect [/b]with our loved ones and [b]express [/b]our creativity. A [u]backward understanding[/u] of what is to [b]Diane [/b]([i]14-Kitchelin star winner[/i]), the opportunity for the highest expression of [b]precision [/b]and [b]skill[/b]. Here’s how we served up Diane’s visuals.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/cf9636a18288d19b60f543ab650fa77a5bacb0df.png[/img]
[h2]Why is Diane?[/h2]
As chefs, we knew [i](and maybe were taught by)[/i] some very mean people that were simply the best at what they do. [strike]Diane is *insert generic angry chef tv personality*[/strike]. 
[h2]What is Diane?[/h2]
	We started knowing we wanted three things from Diane’s visual design:
[olist]
[*] 	An [u]imposing [/u]character shilouette.
[*] 	Her [u]onion [/u]creatures and [u]Hellenic [/u]heritage to be represented.
[*] 	A [u]knife[/u]; nothing is more precious to some chefs – than their [b]knife[/b].
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/f32f39611dbe88b22fa621c0def5e29fca1bf7fa.png[/img]
Unlike our other [i]Combat Chefs[/i], our initial posing sketch had a strong bias towards Diane being [i]tall[/i]. Our only major consideration in this study was whether she should hold her onion, like a Shakespearean actor, or wield it on the edge of her knife.
[h2]Power Costuming[/h2]
	While Diane balancing an onion at the end of her blade was poignant [i](or should I say *point-ignant*)[/i] it didn’t seem like a [b]serious chef[/b] action. Instead, having her distinct chef knife [i]Algae[/i], named after the Greek spirits of suffering, sheathed on her leg was a great way to impose some [b]authority [/b]while adding detail to the leg region.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/e423d54a65ba8ad59f3d25c6addaadbda80e7925.png[/img]
	Additionally, Diane started with some heels. However, going back to our design principles of Diane, a serious, hard-working chef, would [strike]probably[/strike] not wear heels in the kitchen.

	The other part of Diane’s key costuming was her buttoned up chef jacket, long chef trousers and necktie. These imposed that [i]“oh no, the executive chef [u]just [/u]walked in, and I haven’t peeled the onions from this morning's delivery yet 0 _ 0”[/i] feeling.
[h2]Oni-on[/h2]
	The Onion [b]GladiEATers [/b]have some iconic [i]*cry on your enemy powers*[/i] inspired by onions' ability to make some people cry their eyes out (me included). Diane was embracing that by being the type of chef that makes [u]you [/u]cry for making a mediocre broth. However, her design needed to be pushed to [b]more onion heights.[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/35dc4334b5283490280fc921d5bffe3e2bc46433.gif[/img]
	We did this through colour: Diane’s long hair was inspired by an onion’s root, turning it onion skin orange. Additionally, we braided Diane's hair to further that tangled root image. We then added an aqua-blue eye shadow, blue eyes and clear blue lenses, all to invoke the image of Onion [b]GladiEATers[/b]’ crying eyes. 

         Below is an excerpt from our developing comic book, showing a younger Diane growing that braid to the impressive length it is now. Look at her, sharpening knives and peeling onions on the streets of Thessaloniki, Greece – a real go-getter.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/f32d9ceb8ba706123d3bafc9541901266fb9181e.png[/img]
Finally, the Onion [b]GladiEATers [/b]have a unique [i]eye of Horus[/i] inspiration that we then had tattooed along Diane’s sleeve. [u][b]Pro tip: In real life, you can tell a young chef’s power level by how many tattoos they have. [/b][/u]
[h2]Hellenic Je ne ses quois.[/h2]
	To tie up the magnificence of Diane is a lining of [u]powerful gold[/u], on her: belt buckle, ornate knife sheath, glasses and Hellenic inspired crown and earring jewellery.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/aa3a642b5553a03fc982e5b92dc98fa06e5bd794.png[/img]
	We also incorporated [i]the Greek Key[/i] on her chef jacket, a traditional continuous line motif. The geometric lines add to her [b]precise [/b]and [b]structured [/b]cooking style.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ecf2883845b4e1cb3f399848eba287b1c3b6c1c4.png[/img]
[h2]Pixel art precision[/h2]
	When converting Diane into her [i]pixel art persona[/i], we had her twisting her knife through the air, planning how she’ll cut up her dish. Ad[i]*dish*[/i]onally, for Diane’s unique chef ability we have Diane shouting at her [b]GladiEATers [/b]when they drop below 50% Health, forcing [b]more Power[/b] out of them.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/358c758cfc8a286bbf90c4cd62105744f847d313.gif[/img]
	The ability is a fun [i]risk-reward[/i] where her [u]strongest [/u][b]GladiEATers [/b]are also the most [u]at risk[/u] of expiring. The ability is inspired by Diane’s type of [b]angry-accomplished [/b]chef, pushing the most out of their cook underlings.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/27ddcc449f2b51b3437178c76841766598414fe2.gif[/img]
[h2]Was it your turn or mine to close?[/h2]
	Diane’s design pays homage to both her [b]Onion goons[/b], [b]Hellenic heritage[/b] and [b]angry chef[/b] in one composed design. We’re happy you stuck around and are excited to share even more [i]Combat Chef[/i], GladiEATer and mechanic designs soon! 

	Is there [b]any [/b]kind of chef or cuisine theme you’d like to see represented in [b]GladiEATers[/b]? Anything you’d like to see in Diane’s design? [u]Let us know in the comments [/u]or on our Discord!
[url=https://discord.com/invite/Bv9WxvDPag][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/66cfebe3655afc8a7b4d03af2f142e6291d637a4.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: GladiEATers Dev Blog #8 - Combat Chef Abilities
notes.content:
We knew we wanted the [b]final fight[/b] of a run to have some [i]*oomph*[/i]. We also knew we wanted the [b]character [/b]of the [i]combat chefs[/i] to be further expressed in the battlefield. This led us to the idea of [u]powerful chef abilities[/u] that activate on the [b]6th [/b]fight of the [i]CALosseum[/i] for players to strategically adapt to.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/95f81e73066ccfae3a3408502b63488e35b7acc7.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h3]What does a chef ability look like?  (figuratively speaking)[/h3]
 Let’s take the [i][b]trusty Eggie[/b][/i], full of life and unwavering ambition. She believes in her Egg [b]GladiEATers [/b]so powerfully that [u]they hold on to [b]life [/b]the first time they fall below 1 HP[/u]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/14d7a3c332770cf9b74b1cf209973cd44ef64e69.gif[/img]

The [i]Golden Reviving Egg[/i] appears above each [b]GladiEATer [/b]until they are saved [u][b]once[/b][/u], at which point it fades away – great to help players keep track of who Eggie currently still believes in.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h3]What does a chef ability LOOK like? (Like.. literally)[/h3]
When a chef gets into the [i]CALosseum [/i]with their chef ability active, they appear with a [u][i]deity like flare and aura emenating out of them[/i][/u]. This indicates to the player that something powerful is going on!

  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/5c68bb6a85083064e4d234771bb1ad37c84e032c.gif[/img]

These auras are meant to both express the [i][u]Chef’s *vibe*[/u][/i] plus [i]aid the idea of their abilities[/i]. In the case of [b]Diane[/b], her [b]B I G[/b] knife points to her [b]cutthroat militancy[/b] in the kitchen.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h3]What does the B I G Knife do?[/h3]
    Diane’s ability [u][b]empowers [/b][b]GladiEATers [/b]below 50% Health with a 50% boost in Power[/u] = a testament to her pushing [b]GladiEATers[/b], and people, to their limits. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/27ddcc449f2b51b3437178c76841766598414fe2.gif[/img]

 Her Big Knife also moves in time with the effect on the [b]GladiEATer [/b]activating, making that visual link between the [i]Chef's power[/i] and the [i][b]GladiEATer [/b]stronger[/i].
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h3]Could I have one more example of a chef ability please?[/h3]
...sure: Here’s [b]Jemin[/b], the 7th most successful [i]C.E.A.[/i] (CAL enforcement agency) operative. Jemin is all about [i]efficiency, secrecy… [/i]and [b]breakfast[/b]. His ability mirrors this as [u]he [b]executes [/b]any opponent if they end their turn with less than 20% Health[/u]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/1a35a16afc0530fdc0020ce2704d14739418956f.gif[/img]

    Does the [i]CALncil[/i] (the governing body of the [i]CALosseum[/i]) approve this? Well, [b]your honour[/b], did you SEE his blade cut down that [b]GladiEATer[/b]? …no? I rest my case.

[i]*we’re really excited to talk more about Jemin in a future post, he’s just the coolest dude*[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h3]Closing Time[/h3]
[b]TL;DR[/b] Combat Chefs have awe-inspiring talent that empowers their [b]GladiEATers[/b]. They activate on the final round of the traditional run and even in multiplayer. 

Every chef has their own [u]unique ability[/u] that change gameplay and you’ll be hearing more about them Soon[i]TM[/i]! Do YOU have any ideas for new chef abilities, or even chefs?? Let us know in the comments or our Discord.
[url=https://discord.gg/gnMDBFrhmX][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/66cfebe3655afc8a7b4d03af2f142e6291d637a4.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: How does cooking affect your GladiEATer?
notes.content:
As discussed in Blog #2, [b]YOU[/b] get to decide what creature to cook in [b]GladiEATers[/b]! However, [u]how well you cook[/u] will make your creature [b]stronger[/b] or [i]weaker[/i]. 
What’s that you say? "[i]How do you make sense of that?[/i]" "[i]What about combining multiple creatures?[/i]" "[i]There’s no way that’s balanced?![/i]" Well, that last one was a statement – not a question. Regardless, here’s the recipe to cooking up [b]GladiEATers[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/0720bc5c62822b83d7e1897be7dd4a94593b42f6.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h1]Stat Serving Size [/h1]
	We want the player’s cooking to [b]impact [/b]their creatures. In a way, this is already done, as cooking food faster when time is limited means you get more food creatures. Additionally, we wanted to go further as it just made sense that the better you cook, the stronger the creature… but how much stronger?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/29b0aee3015c4e0f7a433ef7a81ac50d89012dc7.gif[/img]

	Given that the player is already getting more creatures, we didn’t want to overdo any  stat advantages and restrained the difference in stats to at most [b]30%[/b]. What we mean is: if the [i][u]worst [/u]Chocolate Cake ever made[/i] has 100 Health, 100 Speed, and 100 Power then the [i][u]best [/u]Chocolate Cake has[/i] 130 Health, 130 Speed and 130 Power. This fixed range means that even in the most extreme examples, both [i]Combat Chefs[/i] get a decent creature and a fighting chance.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/29410380a279e306797df667a21662f9222666a8.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h1]Isolated Impact[/h1]
	After testing, each minigame [u]affecting a specific stat[/u] felt more exciting than [u]one minigame affecting all the stats[/u]. Rather than the Frying Egg minigame’s 30% impact being[b] spread out[/b] amongst the Fried Egg’s health, power and speed, the minigame [b]only [/b]affects the Egg’s power and therefore that 30% has a much bigger impact. 
  Tell me which set of numbers looks more exciting:
                                                                                  • [b]11, 11, 11[/b]
                                                                                         [u][i]Or[/i][/u]
                                                                                  • [b]13, 10, 10[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/1658057bdd662119e73052e1031a505e47d7388a.gif[/img]
        This way, [b]each minigame performance feels important[/b]. The individual impact of each minigame also pushes the flavour [i]*pun intended*[/i] of each cooking game. How fast you whisk an egg will make it faster! It just makes sense.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/d29db31be9c714604027c019791708dbf30b5921.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h1]Cooking Accumulation [/h1]
	 Every cooking step that cooks a [b]GladiEATer [/b]builds up to that [b]GladiEATer[/b]’s stats. Let’s take our flying Omelette [b]GladiEATer[/b]. Three minigames make it up: [i]Egg Cracking[/i], [i]Whisking[/i] and [i]Omelette Frying[/i]. Cracking affects Health, Whisking = Speed and Frying = Power.

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/8ec1fd160f78720651582d35f741b458e5d658bb.gif[/img]

	Any [b]GladiEATer[/b] with less than two minigames will have [u][b]unaffected stats at their maximum value[/b][/u]. For example, a Raw Egg, which only has one cooking minigame - egg cracking, will only have one affected stat. A D performance in the egg cracking minigame leads to bad Health, but with no other minigames affecting the other stats, they stay at their maximum value.

	So there we have it; we’ve resolved the cooking to stats mechanic for [b]GladiEATers [/b]with 1 Minigame, 2 Minigames and 3 Minigames. We’re done right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h1]GladiEATers with more than 3 Minigames[/h1]
What about the case that a [b]GladiEATer[/b] has more than three minigames? Sticking to our previous range limit of 30% that we set on the impact of these games, we couldn’t have an additional minigame make another 30% difference to a [b]GladiEATer[/b]’s stats. That could make a [b]GladiEATer [/b][u]60% weaker than a perfectly cooked one[/u] – and that would frankly suck.

Instead, each additional minigame that affects the same stat will be [u]averaged out[/u] when calculating what that stat should be. The same goes for combining [b]GladiEATers [/b]like Avocado Paste and Toast to make Avocado Toast: we take the average of the minigames affecting Health to get the Health of the [b]GladiEATer [/b]and so on. As example, when making an Avocado Toast both cooking the Toast and mashing the Paste are Health affecting minigames. In cooking Toast, the player scores a C, in mashing Paste they get an A - the Avocado Toast's Health will be as though the player scored a B in one minigame. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/e0bc58efe242e74613c7a31022ee75b760231e4f.gif[/img]
	Man… I really wish we had some block of numbers separated into columns and potentially colour coded to keep track of all these numbers… 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h1]Spread Sheets[/h1]
The part every designer yearns for, [b]spread sheets[/b]! Here we store all the potential ranges of [b]GladiEATer [/b]stats. I think it’s important to share this [i]somewhat mundane[/i] side to the process, as this how we make sense of it all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/44488876c46e6b93cf4f8d185f20e9550ac5f2f1.png[/img]
	Our best way to display these ranges was to have the maximum values, then to their right, we show which stats are affected by the minigame that makes that [b]GladiEATer[/b]. For example, boiling an egg here affects that Egg’s Power. The other stats haven’t been affected yet, so we keep those [u]grey and blank[/u], so we’ll take the max stats for that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
[h1]Closing Time[/h1]
Wow, you’re still here! Given that you are, please let us know what you think about the system. Any problems or even ideas you have for this or other systems? How else could we have gone about this? 

What about abilities, how do they interact with Power? What is Speed and how does it affect when a [b]GladiEATer [/b]acts? Stay tuned for those discussions and perhaps some actually fun ones in-between!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/719864b3142d3d4f91fe47229a3366027d77dee2.gif[/img]

notes.title: GladiEATers Dev Blog #6 - Battle UI Evolution
notes.content:
[h1]The Evolution of the Battle Scene UI[/h1]

         In this blog, we’ll be taking you through the changes and improvements that the [b]UI[/b] in our battle scene has gone through, to allow you to make your most tactically informed decisions as the world’s best [i]Combat Chef[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

	[h3]Take One – March 2023 – All Upfront[/h3]
This screenshot is from the [b]first build[/b] that we took to a conference, [u]March 2023 W.A.S.D.[/u] in [i]London[/i]. We had all our UI drawn up, and we were really quite happy with the character and colours of our UI. 
	
          However… watching people play, we felt they were overwhelmed by the sheer amount of [b]text [/b]on screen. That bar was also [i][b]so thick[/b][/i] that we couldn’t quite fit the [b]GladiEATers[/b] on the field.
	
          The [b]GladiEATers [/b]names were also a first attempt at just telling the player whatever they needed to know, but ultimately our [b]GladiEATers [/b][u][i]should [/i][/u]speak for themselves. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/52d8584fa56349bb6328ff726ed1da5524a9abb2.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h3]Take Two – July 2023 – Icon Cramming	[/h3]
Fast forward to [i]Develop Brighton[/i], July 2023, we brought this version of our battle scene with a few interesting solutions to our problems in take one.

[u]Firstly[/u], we drastically reduced the text overload by encapsulating abilities in [i]cool[/i], [i]unique [/i][i][b]icons[/b][/i]. This not only made the interface less overwhelming but also provided a sneak peak into the [b]GladiEATers[/b]' powers before they were cast… and we only had to draw [u]3 ability icons for every GladiEATer in the game[/u]!! [i]/lol[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/bb997818242dc7fbac34d7692ca116f1e5215a39.png[/img]

[u]Secondly[/u], we brought in the [i]Combat Chefs[/i] as physical presences within the [i]CAL[/i]osseum. Their animated reactions added [b]a touch of life to the battlefield[/b], and their introduction allowed us to do away with the corner icons.
	
A few final details were the removal of the [b]GladiEATer [/b][i]name plates[/i], spreading them out better, adding [i]health bar section indicators[/i], [i]zooming out[/i] on the [i]CAL[/i]osseum artwork, adding [i]colour [/i]to key parts to the text and[i] greying out the non-targets[/i] when targeting an ability. 

	All was well --- until a new issue emerged! [b]New players didn’t not know what to click[/b]! The icons were central but not as central as the big interactable buttons we had previously. How did we fix this? Well….

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h3]Take Three – September 2023 – Space Optimisation & Colour Control[/h3]
	… [u][b]colour swaps[/b][/u]! By [b]eliminating[/b] the visually catching bright gold and light brown from the majority of the menu, we keep the colour, and player focus, on the [b]interactable objects[/b]. Our ability icons [i]grew in size[/i], became more interactive with hover and click states, and [u]displayed their descriptions on [i]hover[/i][/u].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/9c2bbd6c87e7ba5e7e0f0e666c750d9cb3b78d3e.png[/img]
Taking this to [i]W.A.S.D. x IGN[/i] in September 2023, players were doing what we wanted them to easily – [b]success[/b]!

	Next, we made optimal use of the corner space left vacant by removing the portrait corner boxes by [b][i]spreading out the Timeline[/i][/b]. The Timeline received a [i]sleek transparent black backing[/i] to allow more of the [i]CAL[/i]osseum artwork to shine through. An arrow and tiny name label also now indicated who’s turn it was.

In the bottom left corner, we introduced a [b]sprite[/b], [b]name[/b], and [b]health bar[/b] for the [b]GladiEATer[/b] currently taking their turn, [i]mirroring the same[/i] for the [i]target [/i][b]GladiEATer [/b]in the right corner. [u]This maintained the cherished symmetry from the earlier version[/u].

To assist players with [b]colour blindness[/b], we added [b]meanie [/b]and [b]friendly symbols[/b] to [b]GladiEATers [/b]on the Timeline and positioned [b]friendly GladiEATers above[/b] and [b]enemies below[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/3e1645ad451b8d41b3dcdef4eca7b31305757748.png[/img]

We didn't stop there! Another massive improvement was the [i]nifty pop-up[/i] that showcased [b]GladiEATer abilities[/b], [b]power[/b], [b]speed[/b], and a[i]ny debuffs or buffs affecting them[/i]. This allowed the player [u]total strategic awareness available at their mousetips[/u].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/c514d923ef7512f44a40a03ac57938204e6b1934.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h3](Not) Concluding Remarks[/h3]
	And that’s where we are for now! The battle scene has gotten [b]a lot clearer[/b] over time. But the journey is far from over. With more [i]tinkering [/i]and more [i]vital player feedback[/i], [u]from the best community ever[/u], will push us even further in the right direction. Sooo stay tuned and be sure to give us more and more feedback :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/51df9c54e9b8f632e6d810794bcc98c15c708b34.gif[/img]

notes.title: Dev Blog #5 - Introducing Combat Chef Eggie
notes.content:
[h2]Eggward’s Egg-sistential Crisis[/h2]

	For many of us, [b]Eggs[/b] are the first thing we learn how to make. In [b]GladiEATers[/b], Eggs are the first thing you cook – [i]emulating life[/i]! With over [b]13 Egg Creatures alone[/b], we knew we wanted a chef to specialise in Eggs.

        Initially, we thought up a character = [b]Eggward[/b], a [u]crazy bald man[/u], inspired by my own choice of hair at the time, who [i]obsessed [/i]over Eggs. However, Eggward kind of gave us the [i]creeps [/i]and we wanted to go a bit more [b]upbeat [/b]and [b]positive [/b]with [b]GladiEATers[/b]’ first chef… that was the initial path that led into Eggie’s design. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/63f9cee95faad00a318b8a8967742059872d8d16.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h2]Laying down Eggie’s Posing[/h2]
	
        The yolk of eggs has a [b]bright sunny imagery[/b] that we wanted Eggie to mirror. In our initial pose studies, we thought about what would [b]embody that energy best[/b]. Of what we came up with, pose 3 ended up [i]too delicate[/i] of a step for the bashful egg creatures Eggie commands. Pose 2 was [i]a bit too reserved[/i] and [i]hunched over[/i] but pose 1 has [b]such a brilliant skip in their step[/b] that our choice was made clear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/e3b7b66499abf3ec2b1ff3edaa840b549b88ff9f.png[/img]

	Another thing that felt very natural for Eggie was her [i][u]Egg basket[/u][/i], a prop that has that integral link with the process of [b]raising chickens, collecting eggs and, in general, [u]life on a farm[/u][/b]. Eggie’s egg farm origin brings attention to [b]how [/b]food is sourced, a vital part of the process for any aspiring chef.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h2]Costuming Egg-stravagence[/h2]

	Eggie’s costuming started with a [b][u]long maid dress and apron[/u][/b], visually incorporating  her [i]farmer heritage[/i]. There was a lot to love in this original sketch. Eggie’s side bird character was an adorable idea, but we felt it took the spotlight away from Eggie. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/880a763073cf3cdc7267a9ae32566a2848db093f.png[/img]

	Also, we [b]adored [/b]the puffy cloth shirt, inspired by [b]traditional Portuguese garb[/b] - it brought a puffiness to Eggie’s apparel that suited her so well.
	
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/910b5175744eb674823dbf0a0fe7ef5dd5eb87df.png[/img] 

	Importantly, Eggie’s long dress had a great flow to it, but we scrapped it for [i]two reasons[/i]. [b]Firstly[/b], it covered up the [b]exciting leg pose[/b] we had set out for Eggie in our posing sketch above; you can’t see that dynamic leg kick as well with the dress covering… her legs. [b]Secondly[/b], the dress didn’t feel very [b]practical[/b]. If we wanted Eggie to invoke images of someone running through muddy fields chasing after chickens, a dress didn’t do that. 
	
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/350b33faadc27d9d8b36ce2c72ef3712183fc32d.png[/img]

	Our solution to Eggie’s [i]dress conundrum[/i]? [b]Denim[/b]! A pair of cut up denim jean shorts or [i]*jorts?*[/i] felt perfect to allow Eggie the movement she’d want. In terms of material storytelling, denim has always been an icon of farm life. Also, with the cup up nature of the shorts, you could almost picture Eggie cutting them up herself; her [b]go getter attitude coming through again[/b]. A little band aid on her knee and Eggie’s active character was on full display. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h2]Contrasting Colour[/h2]

	Eggie’s hair buns were originally set out to resemble [i]two white eggs[/i]. We did try it – but ended up going with the more discrete egg similarity by letting that be her natural hair colour. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/3a2791e7337cb584cb8024076829171010c17ce9.png[/img]

        It was at this stage that we really saw the [b]contrast [/b]between her upper, [i]traditional puffed shirt[/i], and her [i]denim shorts[/i] come through. We leaned into this further by giving Eggie [b]radiant golden hoop braclets[/b] and [b]earrings[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h2]Story Telling[/h2]

	We always want a chef’s design to speak for them. Eggie’s design [b]tells a tale of family and the importance of food in one’s heritage[/b]. How do we give Eggie’s family a presence in her design, while not actually showing them? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/113f50908016bc6417222f4c96132c12d1d0ff73.png[/img]

         For us, that was the [b]heart-warming embroidery[/b] in Eggie’s apron, done by her sisters prior to her journey to the [i]CALosseum[/i]! Each stitch is a different level based on their age, Benedita, Sofia and Camilla all wanted to [strike]stitch in[/strike] pitch in. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/a35b6d047ca308b04dac50a141b041861aea6e10.png[/img]

	Another key piece of Eggie’s family was her [b]grandmother[/b], [i]avo in Portuguese[/i], [b]Ines[/b]. Ines was the matriarch of her family and prior to her departure, Ines gave Eggie her [i]golden Egg locket[/i]. The gold matches her hoops, so it is both sentimental [i]and [/i]stylish. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/f10e22fd8d7f64d16112c9de3c10eb24733bae16.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h2]Finishings[/h2]
	
        So that’s Eggie! As with all our chefs, once we decided that we wanted the chefs to have a physical presence in the [i]CALosseum [/i]amongst the [b]GladiEATers[/b], we created a [b]pixel art variant[/b] of Eggie. This was paired with emotes for when they are [b]taking a turn[/b], [b]defeat a GladiEATer[/b] or [b]one of their GladiEATers expires[/b]. 
	
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/f176345ee2268f50e6d1ae4a500c540b2fed1ff8.gif[/img]
	
        Thank you for your egg-ceptional support as always! We’re egg-stremely grateful the community’s interest in GladiEATers and can’t wait to share more egg-citing content.

notes.title: GladiEATers Dev Blog #4 - Bready, Set, Dough!
notes.content:
[h3]Warning, you are now entering our design-based bakery & boulangerie - We're here to speak about [b]5 Bread based GladiEATers[/b]! [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

[h2]Unleash the Yeast[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/5f18f9bb5b0b02eeed19dd2409bc175c5eaa6497.gif[/img]

We knew Bread [b]HAD [/b]to be in the original [b]GladiEATer[/b] line up - a food [i]*Icon*[/i] of the breakfast, lunch and dinner table.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/4092bb3c48bfb2f41c2d4bbb85943a69ed220c35.gif[/img]

The line was designed around Bread Loaf as a core idea. Its’ [u]blocky[/u], [u]rectangular [/u] shape was [i]iconic[/i] we thought. We also wanted it to feel [u]heavy, starchy and slow[/u]; so we gave it [i][b]short-stubby legs[/b][/i] to emphasise this weight - akin to how the tiny legs on sausage dogs or munchkin cats make them seem heavier. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/96d1e9da126b17ffc706b3716e957ac9309aaebe.gif[/img]

Bread Loaf's sound design emphasises this with [u]cow-like moos and hooves[/u]. Those [u]deep empty eyes[/u] add to the bread's character of being a [b]plain [/b]and [b]innocent[/b] ideal. We placed a huge mouth where the crust top and fluffy body begin which allowed us to give the bread [u]air sucking abilities[/u]. It now rises as bread does when cooking = [u]expanding its fluffy body[/u]. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/363bfba60d7e8229cd06c1979b6af2627bc8e427.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

[h2]The Slice is (Up)-Right[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/10c840280558c871bb8d7d53798430d53a8179a1.gif[/img]

The natural question followed, what is a [b]bread slice[/b]? Not all that different from a bread loaf - it’s a [b]thinner[/b] version of its big bread loaf brother. Same eyes and mouth. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/69d80ad627c9973fe3edf8bdc03cd9233fee77d7.gif[/img]

It only needs two legs to give its quirky vertical slice body movement. We tried giving it four little legs and lying it flat. However, seeing that standing little bread slice balance as it runs is just the type of [i]cute our carby critter needed[/i]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/719864b3142d3d4f91fe47229a3366027d77dee2.gif[/img]

Their abilities involve [u]headbutting their opponent[/u], inspired by their big loaf brother. [u]Shaking off pesky crumbs[/u] for a boost in speed and [u]taking a little loaf around nap to heal up[/u]. All adding to that[b] charming plainness that bread holds in our hearts[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/7cdd1462825f7fdf840f0c1ec4a8ff80c237c6d4.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]
	
[h2]From Fluff to Flames[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/b914f613a508db8dc9cda635dcd92955958c5ee9.gif[/img]

But not all bread is plain and fluffy. Some have a [b]darker[/b], [b]more intense side[/b] – and we've brought that essence in the [b]Toast GladiEATer[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/5d05ce525c600d8f10c06103963314454dcb5111.gif[/img]

 The [b]charred black crust[/b], the [b]sharp edges[/b] of toast and the [b]smokiness of burnt bread[/b]. We took those smooth curves in bread slice and [b]sharpened [/b]them out. We darkened the bread and added sharper eyes. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/2997dadec7d782b81af4a153956fab68881cc0ed.gif[/img]

Previously, we tried out teeth in our Bread Loaf GladiEATer but e found it took away from that cute plain energy we wanted...[i]and we are so glad we did[/i]. We brought in that previous design take out and added it into toast where that fierce edge was wanted. That little sad lip mouth in bread slice becomes a [u]large, scary, gaping mouth of teeth in toast's stomach[/u]. [b]This crispy toast bites back[/b]. It shoots out the smoke of toast and can defend its allies in a smokey fog. [i][b]Menacing[/b][/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/7fb45d492c7058d38435471a8782822b680c9615.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h2]Avo-[b]can[/b]-do [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ae2803eac2671dec0541349d2405a566fad2df68.gif[/img]

	When we had designed Avocado Paste, we came back to Toast Slice for Avocado Toast. Seeing how it shaped into this [i]sassy little green critter[/i], we imagined the paste making its home on the toast slice when spread. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/9b6a226ab68017843ae806128d9b068dfe99c071.gif[/img]

For some visual storytelling, we thought the Avocado Paste would work great as a [b]face-hugging creature[/b] onto the toast host it’s been spread on. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/dcbe310eb2646e6a9228b90f9de29a514d310317.gif[/img]

Its abilities are largely structured around merging the Avocado Paste's and Toast Slice's abilities - while giving the toast slice underneath an appearance to let the host-avocado story be uncovered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/28229b90243c77ea8c9189474c5354a4e64675f4.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/899f283be744f9ebe3cefb7a44aa35ac33e5410a.png[/img]

[h2]*Flour* Power[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ae3507e4a1e30b7f54d3a35820c90bf1955b742e.gif[/img]
	
And finally, when we settled that we want EVERY minigame in [b]GladiEATers [/b]to give the player a new [b]GladiEATer[/b] - our [b]Dough [/b]making minigame fell short of that. To fix this, we designed the [b]Dough GladiEATer[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/79c150bfedb3a8904183efdc64ece9191d4ca145.gif[/img]

 The Dough minigame can branch into the Bread but also Croissant [b]GladiEATers [/b]so the dough [b]GladiEATer[/b] needed to be relatively faceless so that it could grow into both branches seamlessly.  [b]So, it has no face, just a bright wide smile cornered by floury cheeks. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/2e5dc0e41e5cc560d8a1eed22124610c04daa1a9.gif[/img]

Its abilities involve [b]kneading [/b]itself for a power boost, [b]rolling stickily[/b] towards its enemy and [b]puffing out some yeast spores[/b] that give an ally a nice-power boosting sleep.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/66eb4e1df1064ba46f430a3c9931930bd7f3243d.gif[/img]

[h2]Resting Remarks[/h2]

	With that, we love our topic to rest. We're thrilled to share our passion for Bread and [b]GladiEATers [/b]- we can't wait to feast on your messages and ideas for more flavour filled food creatures!

notes.title: GladiEATers Blog #3 – The Cook Book
notes.content:
Last time we briefly spoke about all the [b]GladiEATers [/b]you can [b][u]command[/u][/b]; but how do you actually [i]prepare [/i]them? What does it take to turn an ordinary egg turn into a Shakshouka monstrosity? The [b]Cookbook [/b]is the player’s tool to dictate the [i]flow of Cooking[/i].


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/0849939762d444c9f58ac1816082687d98c6a9a8.gif[/img]

Raw Egg was [b]not [/b]ready for this eggsact situation!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

[h2]Minigame Selection Screen[/h2]

  When deciding what to cook, the cookbook appears [b]central[/b], showing your options for cooking on the [b]left page[/b], and the team your cooking has created so far, on the [b]right page[/b].
	
Your options for cooking show [b]what you’re starting with[/b] and [b]where you can go[/b]. In the example below, the Egg could become either a [i]Raw Egg[/i] or a [i]Boiled Egg[/i]. We found the best way to show this branching path choice was a [b]flow chart[/b], akin to an evolution or ancestry tree. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/1b71318ab57abd1713f31dc09dcd9be2bb8d1189.gif[/img]

	The team you’re bringing into the turn-based combat is shown on a plate [i]*theming*[/i], a preview of what the [b]CAL [/b]particle will do when it transforms your yummy food into powerful [b]GladiEATers[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

[h2]Pre-Minigame Screen[/h2]

     After selecting a minigame, and just before playing it, the cookbook slides to the left. This reveals [b]instructions [/b]for the minigame, and a [b]preview [/b]video – so you’re given familiarity with the game before getting stuck in.
	
    In the example below, these are the [i]egg cracking[/i] minigame instructions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ecc130a3624e43f3bb373ded0df75e2dad3c34e9.gif[/img]

	We put the preview video in this photo-like border and tape to mimic a polaroid in a home-made cookbook. This is obviously [i]*theming*[/i] but more importantly it helps the player understand this is a preview. 

Before this change we saw players trying to interact with the video – which was [strike]funny… but probably [/strike]not fun.
	
         When the player clicks [b]begin[/b], the cook book slides out to the left and the player gets cooking right away. [i]/wave/[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

[h2]Post Minigame Screen[/h2]

        After finishing a minigame, the cook book appears from the right. The page shows the [b]GladiEATer [/b]you’ve prepared, the grade for your minigame performance and how your performance affects your [b]GladiEATer[/b]’s stats: [b]their health, power and speed[/b].

Your rank can vary from F – S. With S of course being the first letter of the alphabet and therefore naturally the best score/[i]sarcasm[/i]. What a funny convention.

When the player clicks next, they’re returned to the stage #1 - minigame selection. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/e480fea5b3e8210a8b965a6242b00011e79a3ac8.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

[h2]A little more talk [/h2]

Generally you’ll notice the cook book slides around a lot. This serves two purposes, the first is to [u]hide one of the pages[/u]. 

Originally, the second page always showed your current team. We found this irrelevant information. By moving the cook book to the edge of the screen and cutting off that second page, we keep the player focused on just one important page.

The second purpose of the cook book sliding is to[u] help get the player into the rhythm of cooking[/u]. Our testers liked how it felt, the visual cues for the different pre and post minigame stages illustrated by a moving book and a turning page.

The [i]foreboding[/i] timer at the top of the screen shows how much time the player has left to cook. This is important to know as even when paused (in the cook book) it's still good for the player to plan out their cooking in relation to how much time they have left.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

That wraps up our little cook book discussion! Development wise, this book has seen many iterations and (with your help) will probably see many more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/b0af35a56ea2995d83b6dac53a845e44ae2ccd24.gif[/img]

notes.title: GladiEATers Blog #2 - Appetiser
notes.content:
You can currently command over [i][b]50[/b][/i] [b]GladiEATers[/b]! Each [b]GladiEATer [/b]comes with [u]3 abilities[/u], usually allowing you to [b]attack[/b] enemies, [b]buff [/b]allies and more. 

Now, if you do the math (which I did with a calculator), that’s over [i]150 unique abilities[/i] that were hand animated in our favourite medium - [b]pixel art[/b]. Give my compliments to our sprite artists and animators…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

Now, if you remember from our previous dev blog, [u]the longer a creature takes to cook, the stronger it is[/u]! So, as a [i]Combat Chef[/i], with a [u]strict, limited time[/u] to cook every match, you need to decide; 
[list]
[*] Put more time into [b]one or two mighty GladiEATers[/b] 
[/list]
[i]or [/i]
[list]
[*] Spread your efforts wide and get [b]six weaker (but still quite strong) food creatures[/b]. 
[/list]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/75cc6d3a92f52234d7ec0210c6a9586466841d19.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/75cc6d3a92f52234d7ec0210c6a9586466841d19.gif[/img][/url]

The variety of approaches to team building here means that no creature is ever power crept. Even the smallest creatures have a presence, even in the end game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

Most of the [b]GladiEATer [/b] designs don't fall into the classic [b]Damage, Support, Tank[/b] categories. We wanted to give our [b]GladiEATers [/b] varied roles and different ways for you to play them. 

Take for example our Fried Egg [b]GladiEATer[/b], which pivots around the Damage role with [b][i]Yolk Beam[/i][/b] blasting an enemy [b]GladiEATer [/b]with heavy damage. Meanwhile, its’ other ability, [i][b]Yolk Stare[/b][/i] is a significant power debuff and [i][b]Gooey Guilding [/b][/i]provides a strong buff and shield to a fellow [b]GladiEATer[/b], embracing the Support role. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/0aa2fd7064ef84c094e2c8f19f065caefd371f40.gif[/img]

Alternatively, some [b]GladiEATers [/b]take such little time to cook that they’re relegated to [i]consumable-like effects[/i]. 

For example, the Raw Egg [b]GladiEATer [/b]can use [i][b]Throw Guard[/b][/i], which prevents an ally from taking damage once at the cost of [b]destroying itself [/b]– a common trait amongst all raw foods.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/e201687cb3888ceb648c3bbf6bbfe6ee436b2346.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

Hope you enjoy enjoyed this taster of the [b]GladiEATer [/b]mechanical designs. We’ve got so much more to talk to you about. Be sure to comment below and join our [url=https://discord.gg/Zf5cdzGzSc]Discord [/url]to ask any more questions.

notes.title: GladiEATers Blog #1 - Mise en Place
notes.content:
Hey fellow [i]Combat Chefs[/i], Oliver and Iliana here, two members of the micro team cooking up [b]GladiEATers[/b]; the pairing of cooking and turn-based strategy!

Welcome to the CALoseum, where the [i]CAL [/i]particle has been discovered and has the power of animating the inanimate calories in food! After years of [b]GladiEATer [/b]warfare, nations have decided to solve disputes by way of [b]GladiEATer [/b]combat in the CALoseum.

The best [i]Combat Chefs[/i] from around the world have been conscripted in this battle, each with their own Culinary Specialities, unique team of [b]GladiEATers[/b], and Stories you can immerse yourself in. 

Have I forgotten to mention that this also includes you? That’s right! Play as one of these [i]Combat Chefs[/i] to [b]cook [/b]& [b]command [/b]your way to the top!

As a starter, let us introduce you to the game and its features.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/e936fd78f7dc91cf7ee48368588a7950cf2a861c.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]
[h1]Cooking[/h1]
Have you ever [i]cracked [/i]an egg? Or perhaps [i]baked [/i]a loaf of bread? You do exactly that as you prepare food in fun, [b]bite-sized Mini Games[/b], before watching it come to life as a [b]GladiEATer[/b]! Remember, [u]the better your cooking, the stronger your creature[/u]. Cook up a feast of a team before time runs out!

[h1]Creatures[/h1]
You are now at the [i]CALoseum [/i]and are ready to battle the world’s greatest [i]Combat Chefs[/i]. The time has come for you to command your food creatures in [b]deep turn-based strategy[/b]. Your potential team of over 50 [b]GladiEATers [/b]with over 150 special hand-animated pixel abilities is all prepared, impatiently waiting for you!

[h1]Combat Chefs[/h1]
Seven of the world's best [i]Combat Chefs[/i] are here, with their own [b]tales, unlockable recipes and unique Gladieaters[/b]. We cannot wait to tell you more about the special place the [i]Combat Chefs[/i] hold in our hearts in a later update!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

[h1]FAQ[/h1] 
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/9f1079d9ede5bac0aa5586023c413775bc8fb50e.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/9f1079d9ede5bac0aa5586023c413775bc8fb50e.gif[/img][/url]
[h3]Who’s making this game?[/h3]
We are [i]MilkBubbles[/i], a micro studio with a love for pixel art and the indie scene, particularly its [u]genre-bending spirit[/u] that we are fully embracing with [b]GladiEATers[/b]. We are hard-baked fans of creature-collecting RPGs and the nostalgic flavour of pixel art.

[h3]Where can I get this game?[/h3]
[b]GladiEATers [/b]is currently being self-published for Windows, Mac and Linux on Steam... with Console, and Mobile in due course.

[h3]When can I get this game?[/h3]
Early Access will be released in [u]February 2024[/u]! We intend to leave Early Access within a year.

[h3]Will you release a Demo?[/h3]
Yes, a demo will be released [u]in 2024[/u]!

[h3]Will there be Multiplayer or Co-op?[/h3]
Yes, at Early Access launch there will be a simple Multiplayer system developing into an online Multiplayer leaderboard and Co-op play by the end of Early Access.

[h3]What comes next?[/h3]
Our aim is to keep posting updates like this on Steam so that we keep you guys in the loop on development, so keep your eyes open for future blog posts, and comment down below on[b] what you’d like to hear us talk about! [/b][i]food creature suggestions are permitted[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43162105/ba3ca68269caead6ea1a478990044cad09d9c9e2.png[/img]

Click the [b]Wishlist [/b]and [b]Follow [/b]buttons on [b]GladiEATers[/b]’ store page to keep in the loop! Please don’t hesitate to join our [url=https://discord.gg/QUsG3S4N6j]Discord community[/url], where you can ask questions, share your art or simply chat with other [i]Combat Chefs[/i] such as yourself. 

Lastly, we cannot tell you how powerful and influential your ongoing support has been. [b][u]Thank you ever so much, truly. [/u][/b]

[i]Clocking out,
Oliver and Iliana[/i]
